title: Distilled Pruning: iterative magnitude pruning using dataset-distilled data to produce synthetic subnetworks
content: Distilled Pruning is an operational procedure that replaces the real-data inner-loop training of Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) with training on a small synthetic dataset produced by a dataset distillation method that matches training trajectories. Concretely, the algorithm iteratively: (i) trains the network to convergence on a distilled synthetic set (e.g., 1–50 images per class), (ii) prunes the lowest-magnitude 20% of weights by magnitude, (iii) rewinds the remaining weights to their original random initialization, and (iv) repeats until the target sparsity mask is obtained. The resulting sparsity mask applied to the original initialization defines a "synthetic subnetwork" that can subsequently be trained on the real dataset. This procedure reduces the number of real training points used to select a sparsity mask by orders of magnitude relative to standard IMP and produces sparse subnetworks at initialization.

title: Synthetic subnetworks discovered by distilled pruning can be stable at initialization even when the dense initialization is unstable
content: Sparse subnetworks discovered by Distilled Pruning ("synthetic subnetworks") often train to solutions that are linearly mode connected across different shufflings of the real training data, i.e., they exhibit low or zero loss barriers under linear interpolation between weights trained on different data orders. Empirically, for studied settings (e.g., ConvNet-3 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet-10 on ImageNet-10) the dense initialization is unstable (trained models land in different minima), yet the synthetic subnetworks obtained by pruning on distilled data are stable to SGD noise at initialization: interpolating between two independently trained versions of the same synthetic subnetwork shows little or no increase in training loss, indicating linear mode connectivity for the sparse initialization.

title: Distilled pruning selects parameters that yield flatter loss landscapes; synthetic subnetworks have tighter Hessian diagonal distributions and fall into the same flat basin across seeds
content: Subnetworks produced by distilled pruning exhibit quantitatively and visually flatter loss landscapes than both the dense model and IMP-chosen subnetworks: (a) two-dimensional loss landscape visualizations around trained models on ConvNet-3 and CIFAR-10 show that synthetic subnetworks fall into a single, flat basin across different random seeds while the dense and IMP cases display separate minima separated by barriers; and (b) the diagonal of the empirical Hessian computed over training batches for ConvNet-3 on CIFAR-10 shows that synthetic subnetworks have a distribution of diagonal Hessian entries concentrated closer to zero with smaller variance and lower average magnitude than the dense model or IMP subnetworks at matched sparsities (sampled sparsities included 60% and 90% in the reported study).

title: Using distilled pruning to generate a stable sparse initialization enables traditional IMP to find lottery tickets at higher sparsities than IMP from the original dense initialization
content: Applying Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) with weight rewinding to a sparsity mask obtained by distilled pruning (starting IMP from a distilled-pruning-produced sparse initialization rather than the original dense initialization) yields sparse initializations that behave as true lottery tickets at substantially higher overall sparsities than IMP applied to the original dense initialization. Empirically, performing 8 distilled-pruning iterations (pruning 20% of weights per iteration to produce an intermediate stable mask at 83% sparsity) and then running IMP (still rewinding to initialization) finds sparse initializations that match or exceed the performance of IMP with weight rewinding to the third training epoch and that reach higher sparsities than achievable by IMP from the dense initialization. On ImageNet-10 with ResNet-10, this hybrid method yields lottery tickets with up to an order of magnitude fewer parameters compared to IMP applied to the dense initialization.

title: Distilled pruning can match IMP performance on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 while using orders-of-magnitude fewer training points, but performance depends on distilled-data quality
content: When using trajectory-matching distilled datasets of appropriate quality for the target model (e.g., Efficient Dataset Condensation tuned for the target architecture), Distilled Pruning matches the test accuracy of traditional IMP on ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 while using roughly 150x fewer real training points to generate the sparsity mask (example distilled settings: 10 images per class). However, across a range of datasets and compression ratios, the performance of synthetic subnetworks relative to IMP depends strongly on the distilled-data accuracy: on more complex tasks or when distilled data under-performs (e.g., CIFAR-100 or larger datasets with poorer distilled accuracy), synthetic subnetworks tend to be more stable but can underperform IMP in final test accuracy. Thus, distilled pruning provides an empirical trade-off: substantial reductions in inner-loop data usage and increased stability, at the cost of relying on high-quality distilled data to preserve performance.

title: Sparsity masks produced by distilled pruning and by IMP are structurally uncorrelated while sharing similar per-weight magnitude distributions at initialization
content: Empirical analysis of the binary sparsity masks produced from the same random initialization shows that the locations of pruned parameters chosen by distilled pruning are nearly independent from those chosen by IMP: the distribution of zeros across layers does not reveal a consistent structural pattern that differentiates the two methods, and the magnitudes of weights that are pruned at initialization follow similar distributions between methods. In other words, distilled pruning and IMP select largely distinct sets of parameters to remove even when starting from the same initialization, despite producing different downstream stability and curvature properties.
